# Ho-Smart v0.2.9-dev.2 — Default and Ch. 1–4 schedule editor

**Focus:** Fix the confusing numbered device Configuration list and distinguish scheduled zone arming from true per-channel tone muting.

## Why this prerelease exists

The preceding beta showed long rows of named entities such as "10 Ch1: Mode", "11 Ch1: Start" and "12 Ch1: End". Although technically distinct, the controls made a simple four-channel schedule unnecessarily complicated. Worse, the older backend could substitute zone disarming when a user was trying to quiet only selected audible tones, potentially suppressing sensor detection and cloud events. That is not a safe equivalence.

## Fixes and improvements

- Introduce one built-in Home Assistant options form with five explicitly named sections: **Default**, **Ch. 1**, **Ch. 2**, **Ch. 3**, and **Ch. 4**. All can be edited before pressing Save once. Channel sections are collapsed by default.
- Default provides Enabled, Action, Start and End. Each channel provides Use Default, Always armed or Custom schedule, then Action, Start and End.
- New arm/disarm actions control ZoneAlarming1–4 for their windows and restore the actual previous zone state. Configuration edits and overnight reloads preserve the original state.
- Make tone-only mute fail closed. There is no verified HS006W per-channel volume or mute property. Unsupported tone-only muting must **not** be transformed into zone disarming, global volume zero, or receiver power-off.
- Keep previously stored global mute/power-off actions for backward compatibility, with safety checks preventing global mute/power-off while any channel is protected or independently active.
- Hide the obsolete flat time/select configuration entities once without deleting their registry IDs, so existing automations can still use the underlying entities. The receiver-wide enable switch remains directly accessible.
- Keep existing config entries, connection mode and device credentials. No re-pairing or factory reset.

## Limitations and hardware qualification

**Tone-only muting of a selected channel is NOT implemented or claimed.** Only a shared Volume parameter and individual ZoneAlarming states are known in the verified receiver integration data. When ZoneAlarming is false, alarm generation or cloud notifications can also cease. A genuine mute operation that leaves detection active requires device-specific evidence of a writable channel volume/mute field and supervised receiver testing.

The HS006W firmware 2.0's vendor-specific local JSON write operation remains unverified on physical hardware, despite tests for scheduler logic, command response checking and retry behavior. Power-off may disable Wi-Fi and prevent remote restoration. Do not depend on unattended schedules for safety-critical driveway or entry detection until field-tested.

This is a GitHub **prerelease on dev**, not a stable main build. Stable v0.2.8 remains available and unchanged.

## Installation and upgrade

1. In **HACS → Ho-Smart & eMACROS → Redownload → Need a different version?**, choose **v0.2.9-dev.2** (enable beta versions if HACS requires it).
2. Restart Home Assistant. The main device Configuration section should no longer show the lengthy list of individual time and action entities.
3. Open **Settings → Devices & services → Ho-Smart & eMACROS → Configure** and expand the **Default** or **Ch. 1–4** sections you need. Save once.
4. Check **Night quiet status** and channel diagnostics. Physically test zone arm/disarm before relying on it; do not assume independent audible tone muting.
5. To return to the stable build, select v0.2.8 in HACS or use the release-channel controls if HACS supports specific version installation, then restart Home Assistant.
